title: The debate at Achal
hook: at Achal Batala the yogis test Nanak with miracles; he says his only miracle is the true Name (Bhai Gurdas, Var 1)

segments.voice: Yesterday, home in ordinary clothes, and your line, holy in ordinary clothes. Which plain chore did you do as if it mattered? Day seven hundred five.

A fair is a noisy place. Stalls, crowds, music, smoke from cooking fires, people who've walked all day to be there. Bhai Gurdas tells of one at Achal, near Batala, for Shivratri, a festival of Shiva, with yogis gathered there. Baba Nanak came, and the whole crowd turned to see him. The yogis did not take it well, and Bhai Gurdas tells what followed without softening it. Today: the debate at Achal.
screen: `A FAIR AT ACHAL, ON SHIVRATRI.` → `THE CROWD TURNS TO NANAK.` → `THE YOGIS DON'T TAKE IT WELL.`

segments.voice: Bhai Gurdas says the yogis burned with jealousy when they saw it. And the debate starts sharp. A yogi named Bhangar Nath goes after the very thing you heard about yesterday. You were a wanderer, he says, and now you've gone back to a householder's life. Isn't that spoiling the milk? Nanak's answer turns it around: you left home behind, and yet you go begging at householders' doors. Then the yogis try a different kind of argument. Bhai Gurdas describes them showing off their powers, taking strange shapes, doing marvels, and then turning to Nanak. Show us something, they say. The whole world has seen what you can do. Show us a miracle too. And here is the line at the center of today. Nanak answers that apart from the true Name, he has no other miracle. In the same exchange he says there's no other support for him but the Guru's company and the Guru's word. Notice what he's refusing: to make holiness a contest of who can astonish whom. A miracle performed to win an argument is a show, and a show is about the performer. The Name points away from the performer, toward the One. Bhai Gurdas sets that one plain sentence against all the yogis' marvels.
screen: `SPOILING THE MILK?` · `SHOW US A MIRACLE.` · `NO MIRACLE BUT THE TRUE NAME.` · `HOLINESS IS NOT A CONTEST.` · then, large: `THE ONLY MIRACLE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: skip one show-off moment. Use this sit to find it before it happens. Somewhere today there'll be a chance to be impressive: to mention the thing you did, post the photo, top someone's story with a bigger one, be the cleverest voice in the meeting. Picture that moment now. Then picture letting it pass. Not hiding anything, just not performing. Notice how the urge feels in your body, and let it settle. If you pray, you can say the Name quietly in the place where the show would have been. The bell holds the time.
The debate at Achal. Bhai Gurdas's telling of the yogis demanding a miracle, and Nanak saying that apart from the true Name, he has none.
Your line: the only miracle. Today, when the chance comes to impress someone, let it pass once, and see what the quiet does instead. Day seven hundred five.

screen: `DAY 705 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: MILK AND JASMINE AT MULTAN.`

howItsDone: Sikhs remember Guru Nanak's answer at Achal, as Bhai Gurdas tells it, as a teaching that the Name, not wonder-working, is the heart of the path.

match.prompt: who said what — tap the pairs.
pairs: no miracle but the true Name

myth: at Achal, Nanak beats the yogis with a bigger miracle
he says that apart from the true Name, he has no miracle.

fork.setup: you're at a crowded fair. rival holy men have just shown off their powers, and now they turn to you: show us a miracle. what do you do?
options: outdo them, so the crowd knows who's greater.
say the true Name is your only miracle.
fork.reveal: in Bhai Gurdas's telling, Nanak says that apart from the true Name he has no other miracle, and no support but the Guru's company and word.

trapdoor: what you thought: Nanak wins a miracle contest.
what it means: he refuses the contest. the Name points away from the performer, toward the One.
what a scholar hears: Bhai Gurdas pairs the refusal with a second claim, no support but the Guru's company and the Guru's word, the sangat and the bani.

sources.ref: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas, Var 1, pauris 39–40 (the fair at Achal; Bhangar Nath)

notes: Var 1 pauris 39–43 paraphrased from memory: the Shivratri fair at Achal Batala; the crowd turns to Baba; the yogis' jealousy; Bhangar Nath's charge (milk spoiled by souring, i.e. the householder's life) and Nanak's reply that the yogis renounced the home yet beg at householders' doors; the yogis' displays; 'baajh sache naam de hor karaamaat asaan te naahee'; 'gur sangat baanee binaa doojee ott nahee hai raaee'. Confirm pauri numbers, the milk image, and the paraphrase.
